cards.prose: The scribes and Pharisees asked for a sign, and Yahusha (Jesus) told them they would be given only one, Jonah's: *so shall the Son of Adam be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth* (Matthew 12:40). The two Marys going to look at the sepulchre as the first day of the week begins to dawn are standing where that sign comes due.
cards.member_sentence: The scribes and Pharisees ask for a sign, and the only one Yahusha (Jesus) gives them is Jonah's, the one the sepulchre answers.

cards.prose: On the Mount of Olives Yahusha (Jesus) had already told his disciples, who were about to be scattered, where he would meet them once he was raised. The angel's word to the women, *he goeth before you into Galilee* (Matthew 28:7), is that same promise being kept, so the empty tomb breaks nothing he had not said.
cards.member_sentence: Before his arrest Yahusha (Jesus) says he will go before his disciples into Galilee after he is raised, and the angel at the tomb repeats it.

cards.prose: Mary Magdalene is at the sepulchre in Matthew, and John shows what she is handed to do when he meets her: carry word to *my brethren*. The women in Matthew get the same errand, *go tell my brethren* (Matthew 28:10), so the first witnesses of the risen one are sent by his own mouth, and sent to his brethren.
cards.member_phrase: go to my brethren, and say unto them, I ascend unto my Father, and your Father
cards.member_sentence: Mary is sent to his brethren with word that he ascends to his Father and theirs, the same errand the women in Matthew are given.

cards.prose: The word he gives the women at the tomb is *go tell my brethren* (Matthew 28:10), and it is the word he used at the judging of the sheep and the goats, where what is done to *the least of these my brethren* is counted as done to him. Matthew has no second meaning in mind; these are the same brethren in both places.
cards.member_phrase: Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) counts what is done to the least of his brethren as done to him, the same brethren the risen one sends the women to.
cards.flag: Card's Matthew verse is 28:1 but its point is 28:10 (my brethren); prose names 28:10 by quotation.

cards.prose: At the tomb he says *my brethren* (Matthew 28:10), and Hebrews says what stands behind the word: the one who makes holy and those who are made holy are *all of one*, and that is why *he is not ashamed to call them brethren*. The word he gives the women is no courtesy; it names a kinship he owns.
cards.member_sentence: The one who sanctifies and those sanctified are all of one, which is why he is not ashamed to call them brethren.
cards.flag: Card's Matthew verse is 28:1 but its point is 28:10 (my brethren); prose names 28:10 by quotation.

cards.prose: Leviticus starts the counting *from the morrow after the sabbath*, the day after the sheaf of the wave offering is brought, and Matthew sets the women at the sepulchre as one sabbath ends and the first day of the week dawns. That puts the empty tomb on a morning after a sabbath, the morning the firstfruits count begins. Nothing here fixes a date beyond what the two verses say.
cards.member_phrase: from the morrow after the sabbath, from the day that ye brought the sheaf of the wave offering
cards.member_sentence: The count to the feast of weeks starts the morrow after the sabbath, the same kind of morning on which the women find the tomb empty.
cards.flag: Prose says only that the count starts on a morning after a sabbath; I did not build a calendar or name which sabbath.

cards.prose: The chief priests who went to Pilate afraid that the disciples would *come by night, and steal him away* (Matthew 27:64) are the same men the watch reports to when the stone is rolled back. Their own fear becomes the tale they pay the soldiers to tell, and it is the leaders' work, not the work of the people who heard it.
cards.member_sentence: The chief priests and Pharisees go to Pilate to have the sepulchre made sure, the guard that later brings them the truth.

cards.prose: The priestly party that paid the guard to say the body was stolen are, in Acts, coming upon the disciples *grieved that they taught the people* (Acts 4:2) about the resurrection. Matthew shows a story being bought and Acts shows the witnesses being seized, yet many of the people who heard still believed. It is the system that wanted the resurrection quiet, not the crowds listening.
cards.member_sentence: The priests, the captain of the temple and the Sadducees come upon the disciples for preaching the resurrection, the same office that bought the guard's story.

cards.prose: The high priest and those with him, named here as the sect of the Sadducees, are the same circle that took counsel and gave large money in Matthew. In Acts they fill with indignation and shut the apostles in the common prison, and an angel opens the doors and sends them back to speak to the people *all the words of this life* (Acts 5:20).
cards.member_sentence: The high priest and the Sadducees rise up in indignation against the apostles, the same circle that answered the empty tomb with a paid story.

cards.prose: On the Mount of Olives he told his disciples he would go before them into Galilee, and the angel and then he himself repeated it to the women. Now the eleven do what they were told and go to the mountain *where Yahusha (Jesus) had appointed them*. A promise made before his death stands unbroken after it.
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) promises on the night of his arrest to go before his disciples into Galilee, and the eleven go where he said.

cards.prose: These are two mountains, and Matthew does not call them one. On the first he took three disciples up apart and *his face did shine as the sun* (Matthew 17:2); on the second he meets all eleven where he had appointed, and they worship him. Each time he chooses the place and who comes up, and each time the disciples see who he is.
cards.member_sentence: The mountain of the transfiguration is another mountain than the one in Galilee; what they share is that he chooses the place and the ones who come.
cards.flag: Old note read as a transfiguration link; I kept the two mountains separate as the text does.

cards.prose: This is another mountain, not the same one, and Matthew never joins them. On the first he sat down, his disciples came to him, and he taught them; on the second he tells the eleven to teach *all things whatsoever I have commanded you* (Matthew 28:20). The teaching begun on the first mountain is what the eleven are sent to carry on from the second.
cards.member_sentence: On the mountain of the Sermon he sits and teaches his disciples; the teaching they are later sent to carry on began there.
cards.flag: Placed with the 28:16 mountain scene; kept separate from 5:1 as the text does. Could sit in the teaching thread at 28:20 instead.

cards.prose: Matthew says only *but some doubted* (Matthew 28:17). Luke shows what such doubt looked like: they *supposed that they had seen a spirit* (Luke 24:37), and he answers by telling them to handle him and see. He does not wait until they are sure before he comes and stands among them.
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) stands in the midst of the disciples with peace, and answers their fear that he is a spirit by letting them handle him.

cards.prose: Matthew says some doubted and goes no further. John gives the doubt a name: Thomas, who was not with the others the first time and said *I will not believe* (John 20:25) until he saw the nail prints. Yahusha (Jesus) does not drop him from the number but comes again and offers him his hands and his side.
cards.member_sentence: Thomas is absent when Yahusha (Jesus) first comes, and his refusal to believe without seeing is the doubt Matthew mentions only briefly.

cards.prose: Matthew counts the eleven on the mountain. In Acts the same men are named in the upper room, and Peter stands up among about a hundred and twenty to speak of Judas, who had been numbered with them and had a part in the ministry. The place Judas left is filled there, so the twelve stand whole again before the witnessing begins.
cards.member_sentence: Peter stands among about a hundred and twenty disciples to speak of the place left by Judas, which restores the number of the twelve.
cards.flag: The refilling of the twelve (Acts 1:26) lies beyond the verses supplied; prose states it plainly without quoting it.

cards.prose: Mark says the eleven were upbraided for unbelief and *hardness of heart*, and Matthew says *some doubted* (Matthew 28:17). In both gospels the sending comes right after, *Go ye into all the world* (Mark 16:15), so the ones he sends are the ones who had just been slow to believe, and the power Matthew names stands behind it.
cards.member_phrase: upbraided them with their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they believed not them which had seen him after he was risen
cards.member_sentence: Mark has the risen one rebuke the eleven for unbelief at table and then send them into all the world.

cards.prose: Before Luke's sending he sets the law of Moses, the prophets and the psalms in front of the disciples as the words written concerning him, and then repentance is to be preached *among all nations, beginning at Jerusalem* (Luke 24:47). The authority Matthew records on the mountain goes out with the old scriptures behind it, not with a new teaching in their place.
cards.member_phrase: that all things must be fulfilled, which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me
cards.member_sentence: Luke has Yahusha (Jesus) point the disciples to the law, the prophets and the psalms before he sends them to preach among all nations.

cards.prose: Matthew has the power given to him, and John has the errand he was sent on: *as my Father hath sent me*, so he sends the disciples. The order is the same in both, the Father first, then the Son, then the disciples; he speaks as one who has a Father, and the authority he hands on is one he received.
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) sends the disciples as the Father sent him, which is the Father's errand passing through the Son.

cards.prose: In David's psalm Yahuah (the LORD) speaks to one David calls *my Lord* and tells him to sit at his right hand. In Matthew the risen one says all power *is given* to him. In both there is a giver and one who receives, the Father unseen and the Son who is seen, and the psalm says it is the giver who makes the enemies a footstool.
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) seats the one David addresses at his right hand until his enemies are a footstool, the giving Matthew's words describe.

cards.prose: The psalm asks about *the son of Adam, that thou visitest him* (Psalm 8:4) and says of him *thou hast put all things under his feet*. In Matthew the risen Son of Adam says all power in heaven and in earth has been given him. In both the dominion is put under him by the one who gives it; it is not taken.
cards.member_sentence: The son of Adam has all things put under his feet by Yahuah (the LORD), the dominion Matthew's risen Yahusha (Jesus) says is given him.

cards.prose: The angel gave the name before he was born: Yahusha (Jesus), Yahuah (the LORD) saves, *for he shall save his people from their sins*. The one who says *all power is given unto me* at the end of the book is that same Yahusha (Jesus), risen, and he closes with *I am with you alway* (Matthew 28:20).
cards.member_sentence: The angel names the child Yahusha (Jesus), who will save his people from their sins, the name that is with them to the end of the book.
cards.flag: Old note ties 1:21 and 1:23 to 28:20; the pair on the page is 28:18, so I quote 28:20 by citation.

cards.prose: At the start he is called *Elohim (God) with us*, and at the end he says *I am with you alway* (Matthew 28:20). The book opens and closes on the same promise. The one who says all power is given him is the one named as with them from his birth, and he receives that power from the Father, for he is Elohim (God) and has a Father.
cards.member_sentence: Immanuel, Elohim (God) with us, opens the book as the promise that Yahusha (Jesus) closes with I am with you alway.
cards.flag: Old note ties 1:23 to 28:20; the pair on the page is 28:18, so I quote 28:20 by citation.

cards.prose: At the start of his teaching he says he did not come *to destroy the law, or the prophets*, and adds that *one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law* (Matthew 5:18). The last thing he tells the eleven is to teach *all things whatsoever I have commanded you* (Matthew 28:20), so what they carry out is the law he said would not pass, not a replacement for it.
cards.member_sentence: He says he did not come to destroy the law or the prophets, and the closing charge to teach all he commanded keeps that standing.

cards.prose: Saying *Adonai (Lord), Adonai (Lord)* is not what opens the kingdom; doing *the will of my Father* is. The charge in Matthew's last verses, *all things whatsoever I have commanded you* (Matthew 28:20), is that same doing handed on to be taught, so the eleven are sent to teach obedience and not a name spoken without it.
cards.member_phrase: but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven
cards.member_sentence: Entering the kingdom depends on doing the Father's will, which is what the eleven are sent to teach at the end of Matthew.

cards.prose: John has him say that love for him shows in keeping his commandments, and Matthew ends with him telling the eleven to teach others to observe *all things whatsoever I have commanded you* (Matthew 28:20). The charge is not something added after the cross; it is the same keeping he had called love before it.
cards.member_sentence: Love for Yahusha (Jesus) is shown by keeping his commandments, the same commandments the eleven are sent to teach.

new_threads.title: The watch set at the tomb and the story the rulers paid for
new_threads.summary_md:
Before the stone was ever moved, the chief priests and Pharisees had gone to Pilate with a fear and a plan.

*Command therefore that the sepulchre be made sure until the third day, lest his disciples come by night, and steal him away, and say unto the people, He is risen from the dead: so the last error shall be worse than the first.* (Matthew 27:64)

The watch was set to keep one story from being told. Then the watch came back with the truth of what had happened, and the same men who had asked for the guard took counsel with the elders and bought the very tale they had feared, with a promise to square it with the governor.

*Say ye, His disciples came by night, and stole him away while we slept.* (Matthew 28:13)

Matthew says plainly how it spread and who began it.

*So they took the money, and did as they were taught: and this saying is commonly reported among the Yahudim (Jews) until this day.* (Matthew 28:15)

The ones doing the teaching are named, the chief priests and the elders, the leadership that owned the court and the guard. The soldiers took money and did as they were taught, and the story went out among people who had no part in making it. Those people were handed it. Acts shows the same office at the same work once the disciples begin to preach.

*Being grieved that they taught the people, and preached through Yahusha (Jesus) the resurrection from the dead.* (Acts 4:2)

And the people did not follow their rulers there.

*Howbeit many of them which heard the word believed* (Acts 4:4)

The high priest's circle goes further than words.

*And laid their hands on the apostles, and put them in the common prison.* (Acts 5:18)

Matthew and Acts side by side show a system working to keep a resurrection from being heard, first by a purchased tale and then by a prison, while the people it was told to are the ones it was told about.
